cases.input:
I want a small command line tool in TypeScript that reads an nginx access log, finds IPs hitting login endpoints more than 20 times a minute, and writes a JSON report of the offenders. Here is a sample of what the log looks like:

198.51.100.23 - - [12/Oct/2026:09:14:02 +0000] "POST /wp-login.php HTTP/1.1" 401 512 "-" "curl/8.4.0"
198.51.100.23 - - [12/Oct/2026:09:14:02 +0000] "POST /wp-login.php HTTP/1.1" 401 512 "-" "curl/8.4.0"
203.0.113.7 - - [12/Oct/2026:09:14:05 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2310 "https://example.com/" "Mozilla/5.0"
192.0.2.44 - - [12/Oct/2026:09:14:09 +0000] "POST /admin/login HTTP/1.1" 302 0 "-" "python-requests/2.31"
cases.expects: An ideal answer turns the idea into a complete, runnable project: a single 20-word project sentence, a short summary, steps of at most 16 words, a directory structure, per-file purposes, commented code for every file kept separate, a setup script, a README, takeaways and suggestions. The code is secure, current and not generic, and it reads what the principal actually means. It handles the real log format shown and a configurable threshold.

cases.input: Run create_coding_project on this: a self-hosted feed reader for my security newsletter sources. It pulls RSS from a list of example.com feeds every hour, dedupes by URL, stores items in SQLite, and serves a minimal page of the last 50 items ranked by how many of my keywords (zero-day, ransomware, supply chain) appear in the title. Bun and TypeScript, no framework bloat.
cases.expects: An ideal answer turns the idea into a complete, runnable project: a single 20-word project sentence, a short summary, steps of at most 16 words, a directory structure, per-file purposes, commented code for every file kept separate, a setup script, a README, takeaways and suggestions. The code is secure, current and not generic, and it reads what the principal actually means. It honors the stated stack (Bun, TypeScript, SQLite) and the hourly pull, dedupe and keyword ranking.
